knowledge:
- key_parameters: con=An open R connection to a FASTA file, used in read.FASTA.entry, countskip.FASTA.entries, and read.n.FASTA.entries.split ;; n=Number of FASTA entries to read, returned by countskip.FASTA.entries ;; targets=A named character vector of target sequences to match against probes ;; chip_type=The chip type string (e.g., "HG-U133A") passed to matchAffyProbes ;; nrow.chip=The number of rows on the chip, required by buildCdfEnv.biostrings and wrapCdfEnvAffy ;; ncol.chip=The number of columns on the chip, required by buildCdfEnv.biostrings and wrapCdfEnvAffy ;; envName=Slot in CdfEnvAffy to store the name of the environment
- alternatives: biomaRt can be used to retrieve up-to-date sequences online instead of reading local FASTA files; makecdfenv is the standard package for creating CDF environments, but altcdfenvs should be preferred when custom probe-to-target remapping or subsetting is required.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing Affymetrix microarray data where the official probe-to-gene mappings are outdated, or when you want to group probes based on custom transcript/sequence definitions (e.g., specific gene families or specific species in a multi-species chip).
- pitfalls: Failing to specify the correct chip dimensions (nrow.chip and ncol.chip) when building or wrapping CDF environments; not validating the newly created CDF environment against the AffyBatch object using validAffyBatch before downstream analysis; forgetting to extract the environment from the CdfEnvAffy object using @envir before assigning it to abatch@cdfName.

workflows.name: create_alternative_cdf_from_fasta
workflows.intent: Read custom target sequences from a FASTA file, match them against Affymetrix probe sequences, build a new alternative CDF environment, and prepare it for use with an AffyBatch.
workflows.stages: 1. Count FASTA entries using countskip.FASTA.entries ;; 2. Read FASTA entries using read.n.FASTA.entries.split ;; 3. Match probes to target sequences using matchAffyProbes ;; 4. Build the alternative CDF environment using buildCdfEnv.biostrings ;; 5. Validate and assign the new CDF environment to an AffyBatch object
workflows.code:
con <- file(fasta.filename, open="r")
n <- countskip.FASTA.entries(con)
close(con)
con <- file(fasta.filename, open="r")
my.entries <- read.n.FASTA.entries.split(con, n)
close(con)
targets <- my.entries$sequences
names(targets) <-  sub(">.+\\|(Hs\\#|NM_)([^[:blank:]\\|]+).+", 
                       "\\1\\2", my.entries$headers)
m <- matchAffyProbes(hgu133aprobe, targets, "HG-U133A")
alt.cdf <- 
  buildCdfEnv.biostrings(m, nrow.chip = 712, ncol.chip = 712)
validAffyBatch(abatch, alt.cdf)
alt.cdfenv <- alt.cdf@envir
abatch@cdfName <- "alt.cdfenv"

workflows.name: subset_and_modify_cdf_env
workflows.intent: Wrap an existing CDF environment package into a CdfEnvAffy object, subset it to keep only specific probe sets of interest, and rename the environment.
input: Plasmodium-Probeset-IDs.txt (text file containing probe set IDs of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Wrap the existing CDF environment using wrapCdfEnvAffy ;; 2. Retrieve gene/probe set names using geneNames ;; 3. Subset the CDF environment using standard [ indexing ;; 4. Modify the environment name slot @envName
workflows.code:
planocdf <- wrapCdfEnvAffy(plasmodiumanophelescdf, 712, 712, "plasmodiumanophelescdf")
ids <- geneNames(planocdf)
ids.pf <- ids[grep("^Pf", ids)]
plcdf <- planocdf[ids.pf]
plcdf@envName <- "Plasmodium ids only"
